decisions.reason: The scope paragraph denies physical premises beyond P2 although the observable definition (g), Born-law theorem, preparation-moments theorem and state-separation theorem explicitly adopt P1 and P2. Replaced this false premise inventory by P1 for rays/densities, P2 for assigned spectral laws, and P5 for the massive spinless operators; no theorem conclusion or empirical claim was weakened.

P1 and P5 exclude the constant-modulus plane wave and the evaluation functional from L2, but they do not assign physical position probabilities. F3/F4 and Counterexample 1.2/3.1 invoke the outcome-law definition and position-law theorem requiring P2 and AC as well as Countable Choice. Explicitly adopted P2 and both choice hypotheses; retained the cube-integral divergence, shrinking-tent Cauchy–Schwarz contradiction, atomlessness and Gaussian-bin conclusions.

Read Tong Sections 1.1 and 3.3.1, printed pages 3–5 and 79–81: they give the Born position density and expectation formulas, not the stated power-tail example or moment nonexistence. Corrected the reference description to distinguish that background from this locally supplied construction. Independently checked the t^-3 density tail: normalization and absolute first moment converge by p-series comparison, while the second-moment t^-1 tail diverges; oddness gives mean zero and the supplied domain criteria apply.

Clause (ii) calls rho mixed for every w in [0,1], contradicting the supplied definition: at w=0 or 1 it is a rank-one pure state. Preserved the closed interval and all readout formulas, and proved that only 0<w<1 gives rank two and hence a mixed state. F6 now states the actual density/pure/mixed definition; rank-one positivity and trace formulas establish that the mixture is a density. Clarified substitution p=w, q=1-w for all three moment formulas.
